record.what_it_does: AI academic search engine returning peer-reviewed papers, citations, and research-agent analyses.
record.auth_notes: REST API uses an API key sent in the x-api-key header, taken from the second-hand fetch summary and not confirmed in docs. The hosted MCP server uses OAuth with browser sign-in, reported as DCR by third-party listings. There is no documented OAuth for the REST API. An API key belongs to one account, so a multi-user toolkit would need each user to paste their own key, or would use MCP OAuth.
record.access_notes: The API page says API access is included on every paid plan. The plan names and prices were not visible. I did not confirm whether a free tier or trial has API access. Keys are created on the Consensus API/MCP page.
record.api_breadth_notes: Two main endpoints: GET /v1/search (ranked papers with metadata and full-text chunks) and POST /v1/threads (async research agent with Pro and Deep modes and follow-ups). Filters cover study design, sample size, journal quartile, year, and Medical mode.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp is a hosted remote server. The setup guide is at docs.consensus.app/consensus-mcp, and the Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp GitHub repo is linked.
record.blocker_notes: The API needs a paid plan and has a narrow surface. Authentication is per-user API key, and OAuth appears to exist only for the MCP server. The requested OAuth is not available for the REST API as far as I could tell. docs.consensus.app returned 403, so the details are unverified.

evidence.quote: API access is included on every paid plan

record.needs_human: docs.consensus.app returned 403 to my fetch. Please check these in a browser: the exact API key header, whether any free tier or trial can use the API, which plan is the minimum, whether webhooks, an OpenAPI spec or a sandbox exist, and whether the REST API supports OAuth.
